findings.issue_text: [BUG] grafanaInfraLogWrapper.FromContext type-asserts d.l.FromContext(ctx) to *log.ConcreteLogger, but log.ConcreteLogger is an interface type, so the dynamic value stored in the interface can never be a pointer to that interface and the assertion always fails. FromContext always takes the fallback `return d.New()`, which builds a logger without the context's contextual attributes; the LoggerMiddleware's `m.logger.FromContext(ctx).Info("Plugin Request Completed", ...)` therefore logs with only the base "plugin.instrumentation" context, and the endpoint/pluginId/dsName/dsUID/uname attributes that the new ContextualLoggerMiddleware attaches via log.WithContextualAttributes are silently dropped from every plugin request completion log — the feature this refactor introduces is a no-op on real loggers.

[BUG] TestLogger.FromContext returns NewTestLogger() instead of the receiver f, so every contextual log call is routed to a freshly allocated, unreferenced logger. Any test double that captures log calls via a TestLogger now records nothing on the FromContext path: LoggerMiddleware's `m.logger.FromContext(ctx).Info(...)` writes "Plugin Request Completed" into a throwaway TestLogger, so assertions on fakeLogger.Calls/Message/ErrorLogs see zero calls and either fail or silently stop verifying anything; the test double no longer honors the capture contract its name implies.

[BUG] logRequest drops the traceID log parameter (the tracing.TraceIDFromContext block and its import are removed) and no middleware in the new stack — including the new ContextualLoggerMiddleware's instrumentContext — re-adds a traceID attribute to the contextual logger. The "grafana-data-egress" plugin request completion log event no longer carries a traceID field, so operators lose the ability to correlate plugin egress logs with distributed traces for the same request.

[ADVISORY] This diff introduces a new middleware with non-trivial conditional behavior (per-endpoint context enrichment with nil-guarded DataSourceInstanceSettings/User attributes) and no test in the diff exercises it. The enrichment logic — including the FromContext plumbing it depends on in pkg/plugins/log — is exactly the part that silently no-ops (see the *log.ConcreteLogger assertion defect), and with no test in this change a regression in attribute construction or middleware wiring ships unnoticed; future contributors modifying the middleware have no behavioral contract to verify against.

[BUG] TestLogger.FromContext returns a brand-new NewTestLogger() instead of the receiver, so log calls routed through m.logger.FromContext(ctx) are recorded on a throwaway logger that the test never holds a reference to. LoggerMiddleware.logRequest now unconditionally calls m.logger.FromContext(ctx).Info(...) (logger_middleware.go line ~60); any test that injects a TestLogger as the middleware's plog.Logger and asserts on its Logs/Calls observes zero recorded calls after this change, so existing logger_middleware_test assertions fail or must be gutted, and the new contextual attributes (endpoint, pluginId, dsName, uname) can never be asserted because ctx is also discarded by the fake.

[ADVISORY] The new ContextualLoggerMiddleware ships with no test in this diff — the only test file touched is the rename instrumentation_middleware_test.go -> metrics_middleware_test.go, whose sole change is the constructor rename, and no contextual_logger_middleware_test.go is added. A regression in instrumentContext (e.g., dropping the dsName/dsUID append when DataSourceInstanceSettings is non-nil, or the uname append when User is non-nil, or the endpoint tag) ships unnoticed; the middleware that now solely owns plugin/request log enrichment is completely unverified, and the metrics test rename gives the false appearance of test coverage for the split.

[ADVISORY] LoggerMiddleware now depends on ContextualLoggerMiddleware having run earlier in the stack for pluginId/endpoint/dsName/dsUID/uname to appear in the 'Plugin Request Completed' line, but this ordering contract is documented nowhere — the old comment stating the instrumentation middleware 'should live at the top of the middleware stack' was deleted rather than replaced with the new constraint. Any wiring that constructs NewLoggerMiddleware without the new middleware ahead of it (a second entry point, a downstream/enterprise consumer, or a test building the middleware alone, as metrics_middleware_test.go does) silently emits grafana-data-egress lines with no plugin identification; the next middleware reorder that puts ContextualLoggerMiddleware after LoggerMiddleware regresses log output with no compile-time or test signal.

[ADVISORY] The traceID field (previously produced by tracing.TraceIDFromContext(ctx, false) and appended to every grafana-data-egress log line) is deleted from logParams and the new ContextualLoggerMiddleware's instrumentContext does not add it, so trace correlation on egress logs now rests entirely on infra/log behavior that is outside this diff and unverified here. If pkg/infra/log's contextual logger does not re-derive the trace ID from ctx, operators lose the ability to correlate grafana-data-egress entries with traces after deploying this change, and nothing in the diff's tests would catch the silent loss of the field.

[ADVISORY] grafanaInfraLogWrapper.FromContext silently falls back to d.New() when the *log.ConcreteLogger type assertion fails, dropping all contextual attributes (and the request context) with no error, log, or test covering the fallback branch. If infra/log's FromContext ever returns a non-ConcreteLogger implementation, every plugin request log line silently loses endpoint/pluginId/dsName/dsUID/uname with zero signal — the failure mode is indistinguishable from the middleware not being wired at all; the fallback branch is also untested in this diff.

[BUG] The PR is titled and framed as a chore rename ('Renamed instrumentation middleware to metrics middleware') but the diff introduces an entirely new ContextualLoggerMiddleware, a new method on the exported plugins/log.Logger interface, and rewrites LoggerMiddleware's logRequest behavior — functional work with no stated requirement. Reviewers and release-notes readers treat this as a no-op rename and do not scrutinize the logging behavior change; the new middleware ships without its own requirement, test plan, or changelog entry, and any regression in the log-field relocation (pluginId, endpoint, dsName, dsUID, uname moving from explicit logParams to contextual attributes) is invisible to the review process that approved a 'rename'.

[BUG] The diff adds a required method FromContext(ctx context.Context) Logger to the exported plugins/log.Logger interface, a breaking public-contract change that is not traceable to the stated rename intent. Every out-of-tree or third-party implementation of plugins/log.Logger fails to compile after upgrading; in-tree this is masked because the diff updates the only two implementers (TestLogger, grafanaInfraLogWrapper), so the breaking-interface cost is silently externalized to consumers of the package.

[BUG] TestLogger.FromContext ignores both the receiver and the passed context and returns a brand-new NewTestLogger(), so any log call made through the returned logger is recorded on a throwaway instance, not on the TestLogger under observation. Any test (e.g. logger middleware tests asserting 'Plugin Request Completed' captures) that injects a TestLogger and asserts on its Logs after the middleware logs via m.logger.FromContext(ctx).Info(...) observes zero calls and zero fields — the assertion silently passes/fails against an empty logger, or the pre-existing logger_middleware_test.go (not updated in this diff) now records nothing and its field assertions break.

[ADVISORY] LoggerMiddleware now silently depends on ContextualLoggerMiddleware being earlier in the middleware stack for its pluginId/endpoint/uname/dsName/dsUID log fields — a hidden coupling between two independently exported constructors. Any stack that constructs NewLoggerMiddleware without NewContextualLoggerMiddleware (both are exported; the diff only guarantees the pairing in this one wiring site) emits 'grafana-data-egress' lines with only status/duration/eventName/error and loses all request-identifying fields, degrading log-based debugging and any dashboards keyed on pluginId/endpoint with no error to indicate the misconfiguration.

[ADVISORY] The new ContextualLoggerMiddleware and its instrumentContext logic ship with no test anywhere in this diff, while the test file that previously exercised this code path was renamed and its contextual-logging assertions (if any) were dropped from the metrics middleware tests along with the relocated code. A regression in instrumentContext (e.g. dropping the dsUID or uname append, or the WithContextualAttributes call) merges silently: no test fails, and all plugin request logs lose data-source/user attribution until someone notices missing fields in production logs.

[ADVISORY] The rename is incomplete: the test function is still named TestInstrumentationMiddleware and the LoggerMiddleware is still constructed with log.New("plugin.instrumentation") in pluginsintegration.go, even though the stated intent of this PR is to rename instrumentation to metrics. Future contributors searching for 'instrumentation' after this 'rename' PR find leftover half-renamed identifiers and cannot tell whether they are stale names or distinct concepts, making the next rename/refactor of this area riskier and grep-based cleanup unreliable.

[BUG] TestLogger.FromContext returns a brand-new throwaway TestLogger via NewTestLogger(), so log calls made through the derived logger are recorded on an instance the caller never holds, and the context argument is silently discarded — violating the interface contract that the returned logger carries 'this logger's context plus the given context'. Any test that drives code which logs via logger.FromContext(ctx).Info(...) (exactly the new path LoggerMiddleware.logRequest now takes) and then asserts on the original TestLogger's Logs/Calls fields observes zero calls — the derived logger's records are unreachable, so log-producing regressions pass silently and the fake cannot test the new FromContext-based code path at all.

[ADVISORY] LoggerMiddleware no longer owns the fields of its own 'Plugin Request Completed' log line: pluginId, endpoint, dsName, dsUID and uname were deleted from logParams and now arrive only via contextual attributes that a *different* middleware (ContextualLoggerMiddleware) must have injected into ctx earlier in the same stack — middleware slice ordering is the only thing guaranteeing they appear. Any composition of NewLoggerMiddleware without NewContextualLoggerMiddleware placed before it (another middleware stack, a standalone client, a refactored ordering in pluginsintegration.go) silently emits 'Plugin Request Completed' lines without pluginId/endpoint/dsUID/uname; the previous design's documented invariant ('this middleware should live at the top of the stack') was deleted along with the comment, so the now-hard ordering dependency between the two middlewares is entirely implicit and log-based queries/dashboards keyed on those fields break without any error.

[ADVISORY] grafanaInfraLogWrapper.FromContext type-asserts the infra logger's FromContext result to the concrete *log.ConcreteLogger and, on failure, falls back to d.New() — a logger that carries neither the contextual attributes from ctx nor the wrapper's own context, with no signal that the enrichment was skipped. The plugins/log abstraction is now hard-coupled to pkg/infra/log's concrete return type: if infra ever returns a decorated/wrapped Logger from FromContext (or a test injects a different infra.Logger implementation), every 'Plugin Request Completed' line silently loses pluginId/endpoint/dsName/dsUID/uname — the exact observability this PR exists to provide — while logging continues to succeed, so the degradation is invisible until someone notices dashboards going empty.

[ADVISORY] The new ContextualLoggerMiddleware — including the non-trivial instrumentContext attribute-assembly logic moved out of the instrumentation middleware — ships with no test in this diff, and the relocated responsibility is not asserted anywhere: instrumentation_middleware_test.go (98% similar, constructor rename only) no longer covers contextual-logger behavior because that code was deleted from MetricsMiddleware, and logger_middleware_test.go is untouched despite its subject's log-field sourcing changing fundamentally. A regression in instrumentContext (a dropped attribute, a renamed key like dsUID, or losing the ctx-enrichment entirely) or a middleware-reorder that breaks the LoggerMiddleware dependency goes green in CI while production 'Plugin Request Completed' lines silently lose their plugin/datasource/user fields; the stand-in coverage that used to assert this behavior via InstrumentationMiddleware was removed without replacement.

[ADVISORY] The exported constructor NewInstrumentationMiddleware is removed outright and replaced by NewMetricsMiddleware with no deprecation alias, breaking any out-of-tree importer of this package at compile time. External code (or vendored forks) referencing clientmiddleware.NewInstrumentationMiddleware fails to build after this change with no migration path or deprecation cycle; in-repo call sites were updated, so the break only surfaces outside this repository.

[BUG] The PR is declared as a pure chore rename ('Renamed instrumentation middleware to metrics middleware') but the artifact silently expands into a logging-architecture refactor: it introduces a new Logger interface method (FromContext), a new middleware (ContextualLoggerMiddleware), changes logRequest's signature, and changes the content of 'Plugin Request Completed' log lines — none of which is a rename and none of which is covered by the stated, presumably human-accepted objective. Reviewers and approvers sign off on a 'chore rename' while actually accepting a behavioral change to the public plugins/log.Logger interface and to production log output; the rename title will be used later (e.g., in backport/cherry-pick decisions) to justify skipping scrutiny of these behavior changes, so the drift gets propagated to release branches unexamined.

[BUG] The traceID field is deleted from the 'Plugin Request Completed' log line (the tracing.TraceIDFromContext(ctx, false) block is removed) and is not re-added by the new ContextualLoggerMiddleware, whose instrumentContext only attaches endpoint/pluginId/dsName/dsUID/uname — so traceID silently disappears from data-egress logs. Operators correlating plugin egress logs with distributed traces lose the traceID key on the grafana-data-egress event; dashboards/alerts built on that field break after upgrade, and this regression is invisible in a PR titled 'chore: renamed middleware'.

[ADVISORY] LoggerMiddleware's log output now silently depends on ContextualLoggerMiddleware having run earlier in the same middleware stack — if LoggerMiddleware is used in any stack without NewContextualLoggerMiddleware ahead of it, m.logger.FromContext(ctx) returns the base logger and the 'Plugin Request Completed' line loses endpoint, pluginId, dsName, dsUID, and uname with no error. The next person who reuses LoggerMiddleware in a different middleware ordering (or reorders CreateMiddlewares) gets silently degraded log lines with no compile-time or runtime signal; the explicit 'this middleware should live at the top of the stack' contract comment that previously documented the ordering requirement was deleted rather than moved to the new coupling point.

[ADVISORY] grafanaInfraLogWrapper.FromContext type-asserts d.l.FromContext(ctx) to *log.ConcreteLogger and on failure falls back to d.New(), which drops all contextual attributes instead of surfacing the mismatch. Any infra logger implementation whose FromContext returns a non-ConcreteLogger wrapper silently loses the endpoint/pluginId/dsUID enrichment on every plugin request log, with the code deliberately swallowing the discrepancy rather than propagating the contextual logger it was given.

[ADVISORY] TestLogger.FromContext ignores both the passed context and the receiver, returning a fresh NewTestLogger(), so any test asserting that contextual attributes (endpoint, dsUID, uname) reached the logger through the new interface method will pass vacuously against the fake. The fake gives the new FromContext contract a green test signal while implementing none of its semantics (it neither merges context nor carries the receiver's state), masking regressions in the real grafanaInfraLogWrapper.FromContext path that this same diff introduces.

[ADVISORY] The new ContextualLoggerMiddleware — a 69-line new middleware with per-endpoint context-enrichment behavior that no existing test exercised — ships with no test in this diff; the only test file touched is the renamed metrics_middleware_test.go, which tests the old instrumentation logic. A regression in instrumentContext (e.g., dropping the DataSourceInstanceSettings nil-guard or the User nil-guard) or in the middleware's wiring into CreateMiddlewares would go undetected, and since it silently controls the fields on production 'Plugin Request Completed' logs, the failure would surface only as degraded observability in production.

[ADVISORY] The former single 'instrumentation + contextual logging' middleware is split into MetricsMiddleware plus ContextualLoggerMiddleware whose only coupling is positional ordering in this array, replacing an explicit documented contract (the deleted 'should live at the top of the middleware stack' comment) with an implicit one. The next change to CreateMiddlewares that inserts or reorders a middleware between MetricsMiddleware and LoggerMiddleware changes what fields appear on request-completion logs, and nothing in the code states that ContextualLoggerMiddleware must precede LoggerMiddleware — the invariant lives only in the diff author's head.

[ADVISORY] grafanaInfraLogWrapper.FromContext silently falls back to d.New() when the *log.ConcreteLogger type assertion fails, discarding every contextual attribute that ContextualLoggerMiddleware.instrumentContext attached to the request context. The 'Plugin Request Completed' grafana-data-egress audit line in logger_middleware.go (m.logger.FromContext(ctx).Info) no longer carries its attribution fields inline — pluginId, endpoint, uname, dsName, dsUID and traceID were all removed from logParams in this diff and now arrive only via context propagation. On any path where the assertion fails, the audit event is still emitted but with zero user/datasource/plugin attribution, silently degrading the security audit trail for plugin data-egress forensics without any error or warning signal. The code itself acknowledges the assertion can fail (that is the only purpose of the !ok fallback), so attribution loss is a designed-in silent failure mode rather than an impossibility.

[BUG] TestLogger.FromContext returns a brand-new, disconnected NewTestLogger() instead of a logger tied to the receiver, so every log call made through the returned logger is recorded on a throwaway TestLogger and never appears in the original's Logs/ErrorLogs/etc. The fake diverges from the real implementations it stands in for (grafanaInfraLogWrapper.FromContext at pkg/plugins/log/logger.go:47-56 returns a wrapper that still writes to the same underlying infra logger, preserving contextual attributes). Any test that obtains a logger via TestLogger.FromContext and logs through it will silently have those calls vanish, so tests asserting on the original TestLogger's recorded calls fail confusingly, while tests that merely exercise the path pass — meaning the fake certifies 'contextual logging works' for a behavior it never records, masking real regressions in the production FromContext path the suite is supposed to catch.

[ADVISORY] The only change to the renamed test file is the mechanical constructor rename (newInstrumentationMiddleware → newMetricsMiddleware); the contextual-logger enrichment (endpoint, pluginId, dsName, dsUID, uname via instrumentContext) that the middleware under this test previously performed — and whose removal from this file's subject is the reason the new ContextualLoggerMiddleware exists — has no assertion anywhere in this diff's test changes. Anyone reading metrics_middleware_test.go believes request-context enrichment for plugin requests is covered by this suite; in fact that behavior now lives in contextual_logger_middleware.go (whose two nil-guard branches, DataSourceInstanceSettings and User, are exercised by no test in this diff), so a regression such as dropping the 'uname' attribute when User is set, or misnaming 'dsUID', ships green. This also removes the last structural guard that enforced the old 'instrumentation middleware must sit at the top of the stack so the contextual logger is present downstream' invariant documented in the deleted comment — nothing in the tests pins the new middleware ordering in pluginsintegration.go:159-161.

[BUG] TestLogger.FromContext returns a brand-new NewTestLogger() instead of a derived logger sharing the receiver's capture state, so every log record emitted through a FromContext-derived logger is written into a detached instance and silently discarded. Any code path that derives a logger via the new interface method (LoggerMiddleware now does exactly this on every plugin request, pkg/services/pluginsintegration/clientmiddleware/logger_middleware.go:59) produces log records that never appear in the original TestLogger's Logs counters; tests wiring LoggerMiddleware with plog.NewTestLogger() and asserting on captured 'Plugin Request Completed' records see zero calls, so regressions in logging pass silently and the fake actively hides logging failures instead of exposing them.

[ADVISORY] LoggerMiddleware's 'Plugin Request Completed' line now sources pluginId/endpoint/dsName/dsUID/uname exclusively from context attributes injected by a separate ContextualLoggerMiddleware, with the coupling enforced only by list ordering in pluginsintegration.go:159 and nothing structural preventing LoggerMiddleware from running without it. LoggerMiddleware is an exported constructor instantiated standalone (e.g., in this package's own middleware tests via clienttest); any wiring that omits or reorders ContextualLoggerMiddleware silently emits the egress log line with no pluginId/endpoint/dsUID/dsName/uname fields — or drops the line entirely when the infra context logger falls back to its no-context default — with no error or warning, turning a wiring mistake into undetectable observability loss.

[ADVISORY] The traceID field is removed from the 'grafana-data-egress' logParams (the old code appended tracing.TraceIDFromContext(ctx)) and the replacement ContextualLoggerMiddleware.instrumentContext does not add it, so trace correlation silently disappears from the egress log line. Operators correlating plugin data-egress log lines with traces lose the traceID key on every 'Plugin Request Completed' record; the field vanishes without any deprecation notice or log-schema migration, breaking existing log-based dashboards/alerts keyed on it.

[ADVISORY] The new ContextualLoggerMiddleware (including instrumentContext's nil-guards for DataSourceInstanceSettings and User, and the per-endpoint wiring of four instrumented versus three pass-through stream methods) ships with no test in this diff. A regression in attribute attachment (e.g., a nil-guard inverted, an endpoint constant mismatched, or instrumentContext omitted from one of the four request methods) produces log lines that silently lose identifying fields; nothing in the diff catches it, and the very failure mode this middleware exists to prevent is the one left unguarded by tests.

goldens.comment: The ContextualLoggerMiddleware methods (QueryData, CallResource, CheckHealth, CollectMetrics) panic when a nil request is received. This occurs because they directly access req.PluginContext (via the instrumentContext function) without first checking if req is nil. This is a regression, as previous middleware layers gracefully handled nil requests.

The traceID is no longer logged for plugin requests. During a refactoring, the tracing import and the logic to extract and add traceID from the context to log parameters were removed from the LoggerMiddleware. The newly introduced ContextualLoggerMiddleware does not add this information, resulting in missing traceID in plugin request logs and impacting debugging and request tracing capabilities.

The `TestLogger.FromContext` method returns a new `TestLogger` instance via `NewTestLogger()` instead of returning the receiver (f). This causes logs to be recorded on an un-referenced instance, leading to broken test assertions that expect logs to be recorded on the original logger.

From the diff alone, you cannot verify that the assertion is impossible or that contextual attributes are “silently dropped from every” log; that conclusion depends on types/behavior outside the shown changes.

adjudication.rationale: The diff adds new non-trivial behavior in `pkg/services/pluginsintegration/clientmiddleware/contextual_logger_middleware.go` (per-endpoint context enrichment with conditional attributes for `DataSourceInstanceSettings` and `User`) and wires it into `CreateMiddlewares(...)`, but the diff adds no tests covering this middleware or verifying that the expected contextual attributes are present in logs. Additionally, `LoggerMiddleware` now depends on the new `plog.Logger.FromContext(ctx)` call (`m.logger.FromContext(ctx).Info(...)`), and the wrapper implementation in `pkg/plugins/log/logger.go` includes a type assertion and silent fallback (`ok := ...(*log.ConcreteLogger); if !ok { return d.New() }`), which makes it easy for the enrichment to become ineffective without an obvious failure—something tests would catch. This is a concrete, diff-grounded gap (missing behavioral contract), not a proven runtime defect from the diff alone.

adjudication.rationale: In pkg/plugins/log/fake.go, TestLogger.FromContext(_ context.Context) Logger returns NewTestLogger() instead of returning the receiver (or a derived logger sharing the same underlying log sinks). In logger_middleware.go, logRequest now calls m.logger.FromContext(ctx).Info(...). If m.logger is a *TestLogger, the Info call will be executed on a brand-new logger instance, so the original TestLogger (held by the test/middleware owner) will not record the call (Calls/Message/Ctx remain unchanged). This is a concrete behavioral defect in the fake implementation introduced by the diff and will break any assertions that inspect the injected TestLogger’s recorded logs.

A regression in instrumentContext (e.g., dropping the dsName/dsUID append when DataSourceInstanceSettings is non-nil, or the uname append when User is non-nil, or the endpoint tag) ships unnoticed; the middleware that now solely owns plugin/request log enrichment is completely unverified, and the metrics test rename gives the false appearance of test coverage for the split.

adjudication.rationale: The diff adds a new, nontrivial middleware `pkg/services/pluginsintegration/clientmiddleware/contextual_logger_middleware.go` containing the sole `instrumentContext` implementation that enriches the context with `endpoint`, `pluginId`, optional `dsName`/`dsUID`, and optional `uname` via `log.WithContextualAttributes`. At the same time, the previous `instrumentContext` logic is removed from the renamed metrics middleware (`metrics_middleware.go`). adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] The only change to the renamed test file is the mechanical constructor rename (newInstrumentationMiddleware → newMetricsMiddleware); the contextual-logger enrichment (endpoint, pluginId, dsName, dsUID, uname via instrumentContext) that the middleware under this test previously performed — and whose removal from this file's subject is the reason the new ContextualLoggerMiddleware exists — has no assertion anywhere in this diff's test changes. Anyone reading metrics_middleware_test.go believes request-context enrichment for plugin requests is covered by this suite; in fact that behavior now lives in contextual_logger_middleware.go (whose two nil-guard branches, DataSourceInstanceSettings and User, are exercised by no test in this diff), so a regression such as dropping the 'uname' attribute when User is set, or misnaming 'dsUID', ships green. The renamed test file `metrics_middleware_test.go` only updates `newInstrumentationMiddleware` → `newMetricsMiddleware` and does not add any assertions covering the new contextual-logger enrichment logic or its nil-guard branches (`DataSourceInstanceSettings != nil`, `User != nil`). Also, the previous comment stating the middleware must be at the top of the stack was removed from `metrics_middleware.go`, and there is no test in this diff that asserts middleware ordering as constructed in `pluginsintegration.go` (now `NewMetricsMiddleware` then `NewContextualLoggerMiddleware` then `NewLoggerMiddleware`). adjudication_records.issue_text: [BUG] TestLogger.FromContext returns a brand-new NewTestLogger() instead of a derived logger sharing the receiver's capture state, so every log record emitted through a FromContext-derived logger is written into a detached instance and silently discarded. Any code path that derives a logger via the new interface method (LoggerMiddleware now does exactly this on every plugin request, pkg/services/pluginsintegration/clientmiddleware/logger_middleware.go:59) produces log records that never appear in the original TestLogger's Logs counters; tests wiring LoggerMiddleware with plog.NewTestLogger() and asserting on captured 'Plugin Request Completed' records see zero calls, so regressions in logging pass silently and the fake actively hides logging failures instead of exposing them.

adjudication.rationale: In pkg/plugins/log/fake.go, TestLogger.FromContext(_ context.Context) returns NewTestLogger(), i.e., a fresh logger instance with its own DebugLogs/InfoLogs/etc fields. In pkg/services/pluginsintegration/clientmiddleware/logger_middleware.go, the middleware now logs via m.logger.FromContext(ctx).Info(...), so when m.logger is a *TestLogger, the log call increments the counters on the newly created instance, not the original TestLogger the test likely holds. This breaks the expected “derived logger shares the same capture sink/state” behavior and can cause tests/assertions against the original TestLogger’s Logs fields to see zero calls, masking logging regressions.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] LoggerMiddleware's 'Plugin Request Completed' line now sources pluginId/endpoint/dsName/dsUID/uname exclusively from context attributes injected by a separate ContextualLoggerMiddleware, with the coupling enforced only by list ordering in pluginsintegration.go:159 and nothing structural preventing LoggerMiddleware from running without it. LoggerMiddleware is an exported constructor instantiated standalone (e.g., in this package's own middleware tests via clienttest); any wiring that omits or reorders ContextualLoggerMiddleware silently emits the egress log line with no pluginId/endpoint/dsUID/dsName/uname fields — or drops the line entirely when the infra context logger falls back to its no-context default — with no error or warning, turning a wiring mistake into undetectable observability loss.

adjudication.rationale: Diff shows LoggerMiddleware no longer appends plugin/request fields directly (pluginId/endpoint/uname/dsName/dsUID/traceID were removed from logParams in logger_middleware.go) and instead logs via `m.logger.FromContext(ctx).Info(...)`. The new ContextualLoggerMiddleware is what injects those attributes into the context via `log.WithContextualAttributes` (contextual_logger_middleware.go), and CreateMiddlewares wires it in purely by ordering (pluginsintegration.go adds NewContextualLoggerMiddleware() before NewLoggerMiddleware). Nothing in LoggerMiddleware enforces that prerequisite, so using NewLoggerMiddleware standalone or reordering middleware would silently produce the log line without those fields. However, the claim about “dropping the line entirely” is not supported by the diff: `grafanaInfraLogWrapper.FromContext` falls back to `d.New()` and still returns a logger, so the Info call still executes, just without contextual fields.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] The traceID field is removed from the 'grafana-data-egress' logParams (the old code appended tracing.TraceIDFromContext(ctx)) and the replacement ContextualLoggerMiddleware.instrumentContext does not add it, so trace correlation silently disappears from the egress log line. Operators correlating plugin data-egress log lines with traces lose the traceID key on every 'Plugin Request Completed' record; the field vanishes without any deprecation notice or log-schema migration, breaking existing log-based dashboards/alerts keyed on it.

adjudication.rationale: In logger_middleware.go, the explicit addition of `traceID` to `logParams` via `tracing.TraceIDFromContext(ctx, false)` was removed (and the `tracing` import deleted). The new `ContextualLoggerMiddleware.instrumentContext` adds endpoint/plugin/user/datasource attributes via `log.WithContextualAttributes`, but it does not add any `traceID` key. While `m.logger.FromContext(ctx)` (and the underlying `infra/log` implementation) might still emit trace identifiers implicitly, the diff verifiably removes the explicit `traceID` field from the `grafana-data-egress` log params, which is a backward-incompatible log-schema change that can break dashboards/alerts keyed on `traceID`, but isn’t a functional correctness defect.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] The new ContextualLoggerMiddleware (including instrumentContext's nil-guards for DataSourceInstanceSettings and User, and the per-endpoint wiring of four instrumented versus three pass-through stream methods) ships with no test in this diff. A regression in attribute attachment (e.g., a nil-guard inverted, an endpoint constant mismatched, or instrumentContext omitted from one of the four request methods) produces log lines that silently lose identifying fields; nothing in the diff catches it, and the very failure mode this middleware exists to prevent is the one left unguarded by tests.

adjudication.rationale: The diff adds a new middleware `pkg/services/pluginsintegration/clientmiddleware/contextual_logger_middleware.go` with nontrivial logic (`instrumentContext` building attributes with nil-guards and wiring into `QueryData`, `CallResource`, `CheckHealth`, `CollectMetrics` while leaving `SubscribeStream`/`PublishStream`/`RunStream` as pass-through). No corresponding new test file or test cases appear in the diff (only an existing middleware test is renamed/updated for `MetricsMiddleware`). This makes regressions in attribute attachment or per-endpoint coverage plausible and currently unguarded by tests.
